screenSummary.playArea: The object is on the left. Its centered Fourier spectrum and frequency handles are on the right.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose a pattern. Enable up to three gratings and adjust the selected grating or the spectrum’s log range.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Move a frequency handle farther from the center to shorten the grating period.

spatialFrequencies.currentDetails: Enabled gratings: {{count}}. {{readouts}} Spectrum axes extend to plus or minus {{limit}} cycles per sample.
spatialFrequencies.barsDetails: Square-wave bars repeat every {{period}} samples. The first four nonzero relative amplitudes are 1, one third, one fifth and one seventh.
spatialFrequencies.handleHelp: Move with the arrow keys or W, A, S, D. Hold Shift for finer movement.

screenSummary.playArea: The diagram shows a plane wave, aperture, lens, and back focal plane. Below are the aperture and its diffraction pattern with a centerline profile.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose an aperture and its dimensions. Adjust the wavelength, focal length, and grid pitch, or open the phase swap comparison.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Try narrowing the opening to spread the pattern, or swap the phase of two objects and compare their reconstructions.

fourierTransform.currentDetails: Aperture: {{aperture}}. {{dimensions}} Wavelength {{wavelength}} nanometers. Focal length {{focalLength}} millimeters. Grid pitch {{pitch}} micrometers. The focal image spans {{span}} millimeters.
fourierTransform.swapDetails: Object A is {{a}} and object B is {{b}}. Each reconstruction keeps one object’s Fourier amplitude and uses the other’s phase.

screenSummary.playArea: From left to right are the object, the Fourier plane with a mask, and the upright reconstruction.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose an object, filter, or preset. Move mask handles or paint and erase bins in the Fourier plane.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Try the Abbe–Porter preset to remove horizontal lines from a mesh.

spatialFiltering.dragHelp: Move with the arrow keys. Hold Shift for finer movement.
spatialFiltering.moveHeading: Move mask handles or brush cursor
spatialFiltering.brushHelp: Move with the arrow keys. Press Space or Enter to paint or erase at the cursor.

screenSummary.playArea: The diagram shows two lenses, the Fourier-plane iris, and the camera. Below are the object, spectrum, and inverted camera image.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose an object and illumination. Set the focal lengths, wavelength, iris diameter, and camera defocus.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Close the iris to see which bars disappear from the resolution target.

fourFOpticalSystem.currentDetails: Object {{object}}. Illumination {{light}}. Magnification {{magnification}}. Iris diameter {{diameter}} millimeters. Defocus {{defocus}} millimeters. Cutoff {{cutoff}} cycles per micrometer.
fourFOpticalSystem.irisHelp: Move up to open the iris or down to close it. Hold Shift for finer movement.

preferences.title: Simulation
preferences.unavailable: WebGPU is unavailable. The simulation is running on the CPU.

transform.swapHint: Compare each reconstruction with the object that supplied its phase.
transform.narrower: Narrower openings spread the diffraction pattern.

filterCaptions.open: All frequencies pass. The image reproduces the object’s intensity.
filterCaptions.lowPass: Removing high frequencies blurs edges and fine details.
filterCaptions.bandPass: Only an intermediate band of spatial frequencies passes.
filterCaptions.verticalSlit: A vertical slit passes frequency orders that form horizontal lines.
filterCaptions.horizontalSlit: A horizontal slit passes frequency orders that form vertical lines.
filterCaptions.dcBlock: Blocking the zero order removes the mean field for dark-field imaging.
filterCaptions.phaseDot: Shifting the zero order turns phase variations into intensity contrast.
filterCaptions.painted: Painted bins are blocked. Erasing lets them pass again.

fourF.incoherentNote: In focus, incoherent edges have no ringing and fine bars lose contrast near cutoff.
